_note: A dispatch-scheduler plan entry for the FLWO 60-inch (robofast_core/dispatch.py; docs/design.md 3.7):
python -m robofast_core.sequencer_service --config sites/flwo60/flwo60.json --plan sites/flwo60/dispatch.example.json
Placeholders: the altitude limit follows tcsgo.json (min_alt 20); instruments names the TRES CCD 'tres'.
calstage: the TRES front end's named positions (tres_frontend.json); lamps: the lamp outlets of the
Pulizzi switch (pulizzi.json). Listing lamps is what allows ARC and LAMP_FLAT requests on this
telescope (docs/pulizzi.md); MINERVA lists none, so they are refused there.
sequences: the site sequences of flwo60.json an ARC or LAMP_FLAT request may name instead of a lamp
(extra_params.sequence; docs/sequences.md): run with the request's exposure time and count.
instruments: 'tres' is a camera_spectrograph (robofast_core/instruments.py): read out by the telescope's
camera, with EXPOSE, DARK, BIAS and the lamp calibrations; /instruments lists it as a spectrograph.
state is relative to this file here; use an absolute path in production.
When to offset guide (robofast_core/guider/recommend.py; docs/offset_guiding.md): guide 'auto'.
1.5 m Tillinghast; TRES's 2.3 arcsec fiber in a reflective plate seen by the tres-guider Andor Zyla.
plate_scale 0.161 arcsec/px: tres-guider's config/zyla.ini (Andor Zyla 4.2P).
on_target 'annulus': a mirror round the fiber; the guider centroids the spill.
fiber_diameter 2.3 arcsec: the medium fiber, 100 um at f/6 (Furesz 2008, PhD thesis, sec. 2.1.3);
the new front end has only this fiber (MEDIUM, R~44,000).
ASSUMED, to measure: throughput, read_noise, exposure, obscuration.
seeing: the fallback when the guiders have nothing recent (docs/seeing.md).
Thresholds: max_error (arcsec rms), min_snr, prefer_annulus.
